headlines.snippet: Iran and Oman have agreed to establish a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz for ship entry and exit, according to Major General Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council. IRNA reported this agreement.

headlines.title: Leader: Key to solving economic issues lies in domestic production, getting rid of dollar
headlines.snippet: The Leader emphasized that resolving economic issues hinges on domestic production and reducing reliance on the US dollar. Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei praised President Masoud Pezeshkian's administration for addressing public needs amid aggression and blockade, urging increased domestic production and the elimination of the US dollar from transactions. IRNA reported on his speech.

headlines.title: Iran sympathizes with flood victims in Nepal

headlines.title: Exclusive | End to war must serve Iran’s national interests: Deputy Parliament speaker
headlines.snippet: Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad dismissed the US claim of an economic blockade on Iran as a 'psychological operation.' He stressed that any decision to end the war must prioritize national security and interests, not succumb to pressure or war fatigue. IRNA reported his remarks.

headlines.title: Kuwaiti tanker targeted in the Strait of Hormuz

headlines.title: US must end war on Lebanon as one of Iran's conditions
headlines.snippet: Major General Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), stated that one of Iran's conditions for ending the war is for the US to cease its wars on all fronts, including Lebanon. MNA reported his statement.

headlines.title: New weapons prepared for future battle with US: Iran MoU spox
headlines.snippet: Brigadier General Reza Talaei‑Nik, spokesperson for the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, announced that Iran has prepared new weapons, equipment, and technical and tactical capabilities for a potential future war. MNA reported his statement.

headlines.title: Naval blcokade must be lifted before Iran agreement with Oman
headlines.snippet: A senior Iranian lawmaker stated that Iran will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz in agreement with Oman until the United States lifts the naval blockade. MNA reported this lawmaker's demand.

headlines.title: No one will sell oil in region where Iran cannot: Ghalibaf
headlines.snippet: Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf issued a warning that no entity will be able to sell oil in a region where the Islamic Republic cannot. MNA reported his statement.

headlines.title: 1 Iran sentences woman detained during January protests to death
headlines.snippet: A court in Iran has sentenced Leila Abolhassani, a 43-year-old mother of two, to death on charges of "waging war against God." She was detained during protests in Shahin Shahr. Iran International reported on the sentencing.

headlines.title: 2 Iran's Bank Melli remains open in Germany despite sanctions
headlines.snippet: Bank Melli Iran's branch in Hamburg remains open despite EU sanctions. Germany stated that the sanctions apply to the Iranian state-owned bank's German operations, while Washington increases pressure for its foreign branches to close. Iran International reported on the bank's status.

headlines.title: 3 Man from Supreme Leader's empire takes the helm of Iran’s biggest online retailer
headlines.snippet: A former spokesman for the supreme leader's business empire now chairs Iran's largest online retailer. This follows a statement two years prior by the editor of Iran's most hardline newspaper suggesting management would pass to state loyalists. Iran International reported this change in leadership.

headlines.title: 4 INSIGHT Who is Abolfazl Shekarchi, the Iranian general calling journalists military targets?
headlines.snippet: General Abolfazl Shekarchi, who has threatened Persian-language journalists abroad as potential military targets, has a history of incendiary attacks on critics. He was also among officials who initially dismissed reports of Iran shooting down Flight PS752. Iran International provided this insight.

headlines.title: 5 INSIGHT Tehran debates austerity as US targets sanctions lifelines
headlines.snippet: As Washington targets Iran's financial and trading networks, economists and analysts in Tehran are debating the country's capacity to endure further economic hardship during a prolonged economic war. Iran International offered this analysis.

headlines.snippet: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem sharply criticized the Lebanese authorities' negotiation process with Israel, stating it has yielded neither an end to conflict nor progress. The report was covered by The Guardian.

headlines.snippet: In Beirut, real estate prices appear disconnected from the current economic reality, according to Ramco. Volatility in the southern Lebanon security situation does not seem to be impacting property owners, with asking prices for land and apartments becoming increasingly detached from the market. The report was covered by The Guardian.

headlines.snippet: Banque du Liban (BDL), the Central Bank, has instructed commercial banks to compile a unified registry of all depositors. This registry will map every depositor and account across Lebanon's banking system. The report was covered by The Guardian.

headlines.snippet: Banque du Liban (BDL) has further tightened rules for money changers with Basic Circular No. 13837, dated August 18, 2026. This action appears to be more than a simple revision of transfer limits. The report was covered by The Guardian.

headlines.title: 3 dead, 64 injured in Dabaa bus-truck collision in Matrouh
